mainTopic: The גיד הנשה איסור on the offspring of קדשים, and whether the sinews of an עולה go up on the מזבח
overview: The משנה teaches that the גיד הנשה איסור applies even to the offspring of consecrated animals (מוקדשין). The גמרא first concludes that in a fetus, the איסור of מוקדשין comes first. It answers that גיד הנשה can still take hold because it is broader: it applies even to בני נח. That reasoning belongs to רבי יהודה, and our תנא agrees with him on this point while disagreeing about the two thighs. But the גמרא rejects this answer, since a rule shown for a non-kosher animal does not prove anything about קדשים, which carry כרת. Instead it explains that the משנה is talking about a בכור, which becomes holy only at birth, or that the babies of any קדשים become holy only at birth. Next, רבי חייא בר יוסף and רבי יוחנן argue whether the גיד איסור applies to קדשים that are not eaten, like an עולה. רב פפא settles their argument in two versions, while רב נחמן בר יצחק says they truly argue about bringing the גיד up on the מזבח. The גמרא then brings ברייתות about which bones and sinews of an עולה go up on the מזבח, and it begins explaining why רבנן and רבי read the פסוקים differently.

steps.title: So the sanctity prohibition comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier line of reasoning: the איסור of מוקדשין takes hold before the איסור of גיד הנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that the prohibition of consecrated animals comes first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion of the discussion just before this section: in the fetus of a consecrated animal, the איסור of מוקדשין is in place before the גיד הנשה איסור. This sets up a problem that the next step must answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the limbs form before the sinews, the holiness of the animal's body is already there when the גיד forms. If one איסור is already in place, a second one normally cannot take hold. So how can the משנה say גיד הנשה applies to offspring of מוקדשין?

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / evidently: a conclusion drawn from what came before
The prohibition of eating consecrated (sacrificial) animals
Comes first / takes effect earlier

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the ending of the reasoning just before this section. The 'challenge' is that the earlier איסור should block the later one.

phrases.english: Evidently, the prohibition of consecrated animals comes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the discussion from the previous section about the order in which the fetus develops
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that גיד הנשה applies to the offspring of מוקדשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איסור of מוקדשין is already in place first, so the גיד הנשה איסור should not be able to take hold on top of it.

steps.title: The גיד הנשה איסור still applies because it is broader
steps.stepSummary: Even though מוקדשין comes first, the גיד הנשה איסור still takes effect, because it is broader: it applies even to בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the איסור of מוקדשין comes first, the איסור of גיד הנשה comes and takes effect on them, since its איסור applies to בני נח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. It explains why the גיד הנשה איסור can take hold even though it comes second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later איסור can take hold on top of an earlier one if the later איסור is wider in scope. The גיד הנשה איסור goes back to יעקב, before the Torah was given, so it applies even to בני נח. That extra reach lets it take effect on the consecrated animal too.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
The sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to eat
Takes effect / takes hold
Descendants of Noah (all of humanity, non-Jews)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: a second איסור can take hold on top of an existing one if the second is broader in scope.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּר מוּקְדָּשִׁין קָדֵים,
phrases.english: Even though the prohibition of consecrated animals comes first,
the prohibition of the sinew comes and takes effect on them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the offspring of the consecrated animals.

phrases.english: since its prohibition applies to descendants of Noah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּר מוּקְדָּשִׁין קָדֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broader-scope principle: a wider איסור can take hold on top of an earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מוקדשין comes first, גיד הנשה should be blocked
steps.terutzMaskana: גיד הנשה takes effect because it is broader, applying even to בני נח

steps.title: That reasoning belongs to רבי יהודה, but our משנה disagrees with him
steps.stepSummary: The reasoning about בני נח is רבי יהודה's view. But our משנה rules against רבי יהודה, since it says the איסור applies to both thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard holding this reasoning? רבי יהודה. But our משנה is not like רבי יהודה, since it teaches: it applies to domesticated and wild animals, to the right thigh and to the left thigh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 2. The idea that גיד הנשה applies to בני נח comes from רבי יהודה, yet our משנה seems to follow a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds the גיד הנשה איסור applies to only one thigh. Our משנה says both the right and the left thigh. So how can we explain our משנה using a reason that comes from רבי יהודה?

keyTerms.meaning: A line of reasoning
Our משנה
Domesticated animals and wild animals
Thigh

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Whom have you heard holding this reasoning? Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה says this in a later משנה, on 100b.

phrases.english: but our mishna is not in line with Rabbi Yehuda,
as it teaches: it applies to domesticated and wild animals,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין וּבְיָרֵךְ שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל!
phrases.english: to the right thigh and to the left thigh!
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה holds it applies to only one thigh, so this part of the משנה goes against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by asking whose opinion it follows
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the בני נח reasoning to explain our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reasoning belongs to רבי יהודה, but our משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה about the thighs. So it seems our משנה cannot rely on his reasoning.

steps.title: Our תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of our משנה agrees with רבי יהודה that the איסור applies to בני נח, but disagrees about the thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא agrees with him on one point and disagrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: a תנא can follow another sage on one issue without following him on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תנא accepts רבי יהודה's view that גיד הנשה applies to בני נח, and that supports the answer of step 2. But he disagrees with רבי יהודה about one thigh, and rules that both thighs are forbidden. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage of the משנה
Holds like him / agrees with him
Disagrees with him
On one point

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the answer is that the גיד הנשה איסור takes hold on the offspring of מוקדשין because it is broader (it applies to בני נח), and our תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on this point. But the next step knocks this answer down, and the גמרא then gives new answers in steps 6 and 7.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: one תנא can agree with another sage on one issue and disagree on another.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: This tanna agrees with him on one point,
phrases.notes: That point is that גיד הנשה applies to בני נח.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him on one point.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: the תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees on another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה, so it cannot use his reasoning
steps.terutzMaskana: Our תנא follows רבי יהודה on בני נח but not on the thighs

steps.title: A kosher-status rule does not prove a rule for holy animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier answer. רבי יהודה said the broader גיד הנשה איסור takes hold on a טמאה, which is only a לאו. That does not show it can take hold on קדשים, which carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may have heard רבי יהודה say this about a non-kosher animal, which is only a regular לאו. But did you ever hear him say it about קדשים, which carry כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Steps 2 and 4, that the גיד הנשה איסור takes hold because it is broader. It says this reasoning may not work for קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule, that a broader איסור can take hold on top of an existing one, was said about a טמאה, which is only a לאו. קדשים are much stricter, because eating them while טמא brings כרת. Maybe a broader איסור cannot take hold on top of such a severe one, so the earlier answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a non-kosher animal (not 'impure')
A regular negative commandment, punished with lashes
A prohibition punished by כרת, being cut off spiritually; much more severe
Did you hear him say that? You can't assume it.

steps.confusionAlert: In this step, טמאה does not mean an impure animal. It means a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda [rule this]
regarding a non-kosher animal, which is only a prohibition of a negative commandment;
but sacrificial animals, which carry a prohibition of karet,
phrases.notes: The כרת is for someone eating קדשים while טמא.

phrases.english: did you hear him say that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer built in Steps 2 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the broader גיד הנשה איסור takes hold on top of the איסור of קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule shown about a light איסור, a לאו, cannot be stretched to a severe איסור carrying כרת.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the משנה is talking about a regular animal giving birth to a בכור. A בכור only becomes holy as it leaves the womb, so the גיד איסור, which already applied while it was a fetus, came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here we are dealing with an animal giving birth to its firstborn, which becomes holy at the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old answer and gives a new one. The משנה's case of קדשים is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that קדשים become holy first, before the גיד איסור can take hold. A בכור's holiness only starts at birth, when it opens the womb. The גיד איסור already applied to it as a fetus, so the גיד איסור comes first and there is no question of one איסור taking hold on another.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the old answer for a new one
An animal giving birth to its firstborn
Becomes holy at the womb, when it is born

phrases.english: Rather, here
we are dealing with an animal giving birth to its firstborn,
which becomes holy at the womb.
phrases.notes: Its holiness starts only as it comes out. By then the גיד איסור already applied to it inside its mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 1 in a new way after Step 5 knocked down the old answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה meant any קדשים, so the גיד איסור would have to take hold on top of holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a בכור, whose holiness comes after the גיד איסור.

steps.title: Babies of holy animals become holy only at birth
steps.stepSummary: Second new answer: the משנה can mean the babies of any קדשים, since this תנא holds that they only become holy when they are born. So the גיד איסור is not blocked by earlier holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: the babies of sacrificial animals become holy only when they come into being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer to the same question. It does not need to limit the משנה to a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This תנא holds that the babies of any קדשים are not holy while still inside the mother. They only become holy when they are born. So the holiness does not come before the גיד איסור, and the problem goes away for all babies of קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; introduces another answer
The babies of sacrificial animals
When they come into being, at birth

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain how the גיד איסור applies to קדשים: either a בכור, or the babies of any קדשים, which only become holy at birth.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
the babies of sacrificial animals
become holy only when they come into being.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer next to Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the תנא's view about when holiness starts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The babies of קדשים are holy from the womb, before the גיד איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are holy only from birth, so the גיד איסור is not blocked.

steps.title: Only for holy animals that are eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף limits the משנה: the גיד הנשה איסור applies only to קדשים that are eaten, not to קדשים that are not eaten, like an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said: They taught this only about sacrificial animals that are eaten. But sacrificial animals that are not eaten do not have the גיד איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: which kinds of קדשים the משנה's rule covers. רבי חייא בר יוסף gives a limited view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some קדשים, like a שלמים, are eaten, and some, like an עולה, are burned completely. רבי חייא בר יוסף says the גיד איסור applies only to the ones that are eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about...; limits a rule
Sacrificial animals that are eaten, like a שלמים
Sacrificial animals that are not eaten, like an עולה
Applies

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef said:
They taught this only about sacrificial animals that are eaten,
but sacrificial animals that are not eaten,
the prohibition of the sciatic nerve does not apply to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the גיד איסור takes hold on קדשים to which קדשים it covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גיד הנשה איסור applies only to קדשים that are eaten.

steps.title: For all holy animals, eaten or not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: the גיד הנשה איסור applies both to קדשים that are eaten and to קדשים that are not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Both sacrificial animals that are eaten and sacrificial animals that are not eaten have the גיד איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view of רבי חייא בר יוסף. This sets up a מחלוקת the גמרא will now discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, it does not matter whether the קרבן is eaten. Even an עולה, which is burned completely, still has the גיד הנשה איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; the rule covers both

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת decides whether the גיד איסור depends on the animal being eaten, and it sets up the next part of the sugya.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Both sacrificial animals that are eaten
and sacrificial animals that are not eaten,
the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי חייא בר יוסף in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גיד הנשה איסור applies to all קדשים, whether eaten or not.

steps.title: רב פפא: Both are right, but about different things (first version)
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רבי חייא בר יוסף and רבי יוחנן do not argue. רבי יוחנן means a person who eats the גיד of an עולה gets מלקות. רבי חייא בר יוסף means the גיד does not need to be removed before the עולה goes up on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They do not argue. One is talking about giving lashes, and the other is talking about bringing it up on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the argument from Steps 8 and 9 by saying each אמורא is talking about a different area of the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the גיד איסור applies to קדשים that are not eaten. רב פפא explains this means that someone who eats the גיד of an עולה gets מלקות. רבי חייא בר יוסף said it does not apply. רב פפא explains this means the עולה can go up on the מזבח with the גיד still in it, because burning it is not eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not argue. Two opinions that looked opposite are shown to fit together.
Here... here. Each opinion is about a different case.
To give him מלקות (lashes).
To bring it up onto the מזבח.

steps.confusionAlert: The text just says 'here' and 'here' without names. The first 'here' (lashes) is רבי יוחנן's view, and the second 'here' (bringing it up) is רבי חייא בר יוסף's view.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: And they do not argue,
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי חייא בר יוסף and רבי יוחנן from the last two steps.

phrases.english: here – it is about giving him lashes,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן: someone who eats the גיד of an עולה gets lashes.

phrases.english: here – it is about bringing it up on the altar.
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא בר יוסף: the עולה goes up with the גיד still inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the disagreement between Step 8 and Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split cases (each opinion is about a different area of law)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא בר יוסף and רבי יוחנן seemed to argue directly about whether the גיד איסור applies to an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating the גיד of an עולה brings מלקות, but the עולה may be burned with the גיד still in it.

steps.title: רב פפא's reconciliation (second version): Removing the גיד vs. burning it once it is out
steps.stepSummary: A second report of רב פפא's answer. One opinion means you do not have to take the גיד out of an עולה. The other means that once it has been taken out, you may not bring it up on the מזבח by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב פפא said: They do not argue. One is talking about taking it out, and the other is talking about bringing it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how רב פפא settled the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבי חייא בר יוסף means you are not required to remove the גיד before burning the עולה. רבי יוחנן means that if the גיד was removed anyway, it may not be put on the מזבח by itself. Unlike the first version, both sides here are about the מזבח, not about מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: To pull it out, meaning to remove the גיד from the thigh.

phrases.english: There are those who say, Rav Pappa said:
And they do not argue –
here it is about removing it,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא בר יוסף: you do not need to take the גיד out before burning the עולה.

phrases.english: and here it is about bringing it up.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן: once the גיד has been taken out, it may not go up on the מזבח by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רב פפא's answer from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split cases (attached גיד vs. removed גיד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two אמוראים seemed to argue about whether the גיד איסור applies to an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: You do not have to remove the גיד from an עולה, but a גיד that was removed may not be burned on the מזבח by itself.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: They really do argue about bringing it up on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects רב פפא's approach. He says the two אמוראים truly disagree about whether the גיד may go up on the מזבח with the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They argue about bringing it up on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא says there is a real argument. It is about whether the גיד goes up on the מזבח with the עולה while it is still attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said the two opinions fit together. רב נחמן בר יצחק says they argue directly about the same case. One holds the גיד goes up together with the עולה, and the other holds it does not. He now brings a ברייתא as the background to their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue. Here it means a real disagreement.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They argue about bringing it up on the altar,
phrases.notes: He means even when the גיד is still attached to the thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לְהַעֲלוֹתוֹ פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא's claim in Steps 10–11 that there is no real argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא בר יוסף and רבי יוחנן truly disagree about whether the גיד of an עולה goes up on the מזבח.

steps.title: The ברייתא: What goes up on the מזבח with an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'הכל' that bones, sinews, horns and hooves are burned with the עולה. A second פסוק teaches that this is only while they are still attached, not after they come off.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And the כהן shall burn it all on the מזבח' includes the bones, sinews, horns and hooves. You might think this applies even if they came off. So the פסוק says: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the background for רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement. It sets out which parts of an עולה go up on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הכל' (all) adds parts that are not meat: bones, sinews, horns and hooves. These go up only while they are still attached to the meat. Once they come off, the words 'the flesh and the blood' limit what is offered. Since the גיד הנשה is a sinew, this ברייתא is the starting point for the argument about whether it goes up.

keyTerms.meaning: To include. A word in the פסוק adds something extra.
The sinews.
One might think. It brings up a possible mistake.
They came off, meaning they became separated from the meat.
The פסוק teaches. It brings a פסוק that answers the 'one might think'.

steps.whatToRemember: Bones, sinews, horns and hooves go up on the מזבח with an עולה only while they are attached. Once they come off, they do not. The argument about the גיד הנשה is built on this rule.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
'And the priest shall burn it all on the altar' –
to include the bones and the sinews
and the horns and the hooves.
One might think even if they came off,
the verse teaches:
'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֹּל הַמִּזְבֵּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source background for רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that they argue about bringing the גיד up.
steps.raayaObject: The argument over whether the גיד goes up on the מזבח with the עולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 1:9 and דברים 12:27: attached sinews go up, but parts that came off do not.

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes: attached parts go up, detached parts come down
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its reading. You might think the sinews and bones should be pulled out before the meat goes up, but 'הכל' teaches they are burned too. The two פסוקים are settled: attached parts go up, and detached parts come down even from the top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only the flesh and blood go on the מזבח, maybe you should pull out the sinews and bones and bring up just the meat? The פסוק says 'the כהן shall burn it all.' So how do both פסוקים fit? If they are attached, they go up. If they came off, they come down, even from the top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the ברייתא it started quoting in the last step. It shows how the two פסוקים fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'flesh and blood' פסוק could make you think only meat belongs on the מזבח. The word 'הכל' pushes back and includes sinews and bones. The answer splits the cases: attached parts go up, detached parts do not, even if they are already on top of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: He should pull out or remove
How so? (how do the two sources fit together)
Attached (still connected to the meat)
If they came off, they come down

phrases.english: If it is only flesh and blood [that go on the altar],
one might think he should pull out the sinews and bones
and bring up only the meat onto the altar?
The verse teaches:
"And the priest shall burn it all on the altar."
How so?
If they are attached, they go up;

phrases.aramaic: פֵּרְשׁוּ, אֲפִילּוּ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ – יֵרְדוּ.
phrases.english: if they came off, even if they are on top of the altar, they come down.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֹּל הַמִּזְבֵּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That sinews and bones go up with the עולה only while attached (this bears on רב נחמן בר יצחק's discussion of the גיד going up)
steps.whatToRemember: Rule of this ברייתא: attached, they go up; detached, they come down, even from the top of the מזבח.

steps.title: Who holds that detached parts come down?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view in our ברייתא, that detached parts must come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא you heard saying that if they came off, they come down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion our ברייתא follows. This sets up the next step, where it names the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question hints that not all תנאים agree with 'פרשו ירדו.' The גמרא wants to tie the rule to a known authority and show there is a disagreement behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period
Whom you heard (known to hold this view)

phrases.english: And who is the tanna that you heard
who says, 'if they came off, they come down'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the ברייתא just quoted.

steps.title: It is רבי; first opinion of the proof ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי. The proof is a ברייתא whose first opinion says 'הכל' includes bones, sinews, horns and hooves, even after they come off. רבי will argue on that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי, as a ברייתא teaches: 'The כהן shall burn it all' includes the bones, sinews, horns and hooves, even if they came off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the view belongs to רבי. It starts quoting a ברייתא, which first gives the opposite opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion reads 'הכל' as a wide inclusion: even detached bones and sinews are burned. That clashes with 'פרשו ירדו.' So the תנא of our ברייתא cannot be this first opinion, and the end of this ברייתא will show it is רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
Horns
Hooves

steps.confusionAlert: The words right after 'רבי היא, דתניא' are NOT רבי's view. They are the first opinion in the ברייתא. רבי's own words come later, at 'רבי אומר.'

phrases.english: It is Rabbi, as it was taught:
"And the priest shall burn it all"
comes to include the bones and the sinews
and the horns and the hooves,
and even if they came off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 and opens the proof ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view is רבי's, shown through a ברייתא where an anonymous first opinion holds that even detached parts are burned.

steps.title: What about the 'flesh and blood' פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, the first opinion is challenged. If even detached bones and sinews go up, what does 'your עולות, the flesh and the blood' come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, how do I fulfill 'And you shall offer your עולות, the flesh and the blood'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own first opinion. If everything goes up, the פסוק that mentions only flesh and blood seems to have no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'flesh and blood' פסוק sounds like it limits what goes on the מזבח. If 'הכל' includes even detached parts, that limit seems to disappear, so the first opinion must explain what the פסוק is for.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I fulfill (what does this פסוק mean, then)?
Your burnt offerings

phrases.english: But then, how do I fulfill
"And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first opinion just stated in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion's reading of 'הכל' as including even detached parts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everything goes up, the limiting פסוק 'הבשר והדם' has no job.

steps.title: The פסוק is about pieces that jump off the fire
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion answers that the 'flesh and blood' פסוק is about pieces that jump off the fire. Partly burned meat is put back, but partly burned sinews and bones are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about pieces that jump off. How so? Partly burned meat you put back, but partly burned sinews and bones you do not put back.
steps.whatsHappening: The first opinion gives the 'flesh and blood' פסוק a narrower job, so it no longer clashes with 'הכל.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, the limit in the פסוק does not decide what goes up in the first place. It only decides what gets put back after it jumps off the fire. Meat goes back, while sinews and bones that jumped off stay down.

keyTerms.meaning: Pieces that jump or pop off the fire
Partly burned remains
Put back (onto the fire)

phrases.english: It is about pieces that jump off.
How so?
Partly burned meat, you put back,
but you do not put back
partly burned sinews and bones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the limiting פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'flesh and blood' פסוק limits what may go up at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only limits what gets put back after jumping off the fire. Meat goes back; sinews and bones do not.

steps.title: רבי: attached parts go up, detached parts come down
steps.stepSummary: רבי says one פסוק includes and the other excludes. They fit together this way: attached parts go up, and detached parts come down even from the top of the מזבח. This is the same wording as our ברייתא, proving it follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: one פסוק says 'the כהן shall burn it all,' which includes; another says 'your עולות, the flesh and the blood,' which excludes. How so? If attached, they go up. If they came off, even from the top of the מזבח, they come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his own view, which disagrees with the first opinion. His words match our ברייתא exactly, which answers the question 'who is the תנא.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion used the limiting פסוק only for pieces that jump off. רבי uses it to limit what goes up at all: detached sinews and bones are excluded. Since his rule is word for word the ending of our ברייתא, that ברייתא follows רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: One פסוק says (introducing two פסוקים that seem to clash)
It included (widened the rule)
It excluded (narrowed the rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion: even detached parts go up, and the 'flesh and blood' פסוק is only about pieces that jump off. רבי: detached parts come down. Our ברייתא ('פרשו ירדו') follows רבי.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: One verse says
"And the priest shall burn it all," which includes;
and another verse says
"And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood," which excludes.
How so?
If they are attached, they go up;

phrases.aramaic: פֵּרְשׁוּ – אֲפִילּוּ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ יֵרְדוּ.
phrases.english: if they came off, even if they are on top of the altar, they come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי's opposing view in the same ברייתא, completing the proof that answers step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attached sinews and bones go up with the עולה; once detached, they come down even from the top of the מזבח.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the rule 'פרשו ירדו' specifically to רבי, so the earlier ברייתא is not everyone's view, since the first opinion holds that even detached parts are burned.

steps.title: Why רבנן say the word 'הכל' is about detached parts
steps.stepSummary: רבנן hold that attached bones and sinews need no פסוק, just like the head of an עולה, which has bones and still goes up. So the extra word must be teaching about parts that came off.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן: for attached bones and sinews, no פסוק was needed to include them. It is just like the head of an עולה. A פסוק was only needed for parts that came off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבנן read the פסוקים the way they do. They say attached bones and sinews obviously go up, so the extra word 'הכל' must be talking about pieces that came off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head of an עולה is full of bones, and the תורה clearly says it is burned on the מזבח. So we already know that bones and sinews attached to the meat go up. That leaves the inclusive word 'הכל' free to teach something new: even detached bones and sinews go up.

keyTerms.meaning: To include: to add something into a rule through a פסוק
Just like: a comparison to a known case
The head of an עולה, which has many bones and is burned on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the root of the מחלוקת. Both sides agree attached parts go up. They argue about what the extra word in the פסוק comes to teach.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: attached ones
no verse was needed to include them,
just like the head of a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: The head is full of bones, and the פסוק says it goes on the fire (ויקרא 1:8).

phrases.english: when a verse was needed, it was for ones that came off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, מְחוּבָּרִין לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving our ברייתא follows רבי, the גמרא explains the reasoning of each side, starting with רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attached bones and sinews go up without needing a פסוק, as the head of an עולה shows. The inclusive word 'הכל' teaches that even detached bones and sinews go up.

steps.title: רבי's reasoning begins: attached parts that are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain רבי's side. It starts with attached parts that are 'permitted', and the sentence continues after this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי: attached parts that are of the permitted kind...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to explain רבי's reasoning. This is only the opening of the sentence, so it is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן said attached parts are obvious, like the head of an עולה. רבי's explanation starts by focusing on attached parts that are 'permitted'. This hints that he sees a reason a פסוק would be needed after all. The full reasoning comes in the continuation of the sentence.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the permitted kind: parts that are allowed, as opposed to forbidden ones

phrases.english: And Rabbi: attached ones that are permitted
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here; רבי's full reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבנן's reasoning, the גמרא begins giving רבי's reasoning for the opposite reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The opening of רבי's explanation, which deals with attached parts of the permitted kind. The ruling is completed in the continuation.
